name: John F. Kennedy International Airport
notes: New York International Airport, Anderson Field ('Idlewild'), on Jamaica Bay fill: 'The first flight from Idlewild was on July 1, 1948'. Runways 13L/31R and 13R/31L from the opening ('31L ... opened soon after the rest of the airport'); 4L/22R June 1949 and 4R/22L 1959 dated on their own (data/manual/airports/pavement_dates.csv). Taxiways, aprons and runway lengthenings are NOT dated on their own: all from 1948 (estimated), and not before their fill (terrain land-year).

name: LaGuardia Airport
notes: 'dedicated on October 15, 1939, as the New York Municipal Airport, and opened for business on December 2 of that year', on fill around the North Beach airfield (seaplane base / Glenn H. Curtiss Airport 1929, Municipal Airport 2 1935). The runway decks over Flushing Bay and Bowery Bay (1960s) are not dated on their own (estimated; they wait for the terrain's land year where it has one).

name: Floyd Bennett Field
notes: New York's first municipal airport, on fill at Barren Island: 'dedicated on June 26, 1930, and officially opened to commercial flights on May 23, 1931'; Naval Air Station New York from 1941, decommissioning begun 4 April 1970, to the National Park Service (Gateway NRA) 1972 — closed as an airfield 1971 (estimated within 1970-72). Outline: data/manual/airports/extra_outlines.geojson; runways dated by data/manual/airports/pavement_dates.csv (1931 / 1938 / 1942). The concrete is still there (park roads): pavement does not end in 1971.

name: NYPD Air Operations Heliport (Floyd Bennett Field)
notes: Apron of the former Coast Guard Air Station Brooklyn on the Jamaica Bay side of Floyd Bennett Field: 'In 1937, the Coast Guard built a hangar on the Jamaica Bay coast'; Coast Guard helicopters until 1998, then the NYPD Aviation Unit.

name: West 30th Street Heliport
notes: 'Originally constructed by the Port of New York Authority (PA) in 1956' on the Hudson shore (lease approved 28 June 1956).

name: Downtown Manhattan Heliport
notes: Pier 6, East River: 'The Downtown Manhattan Heliport opened on December 8, 1960'; rebuilt 1983-87 (the rebuilt deck is what is drawn, from 1960: estimated).

name: East 34th Street Heliport
notes: 'The heliport opened on June 16, 1972'.

name: Flushing Airport
notes: College Point: 'constructed atop 250 acres of wetlands beginning in 1927. The airport opened two years later, in May 1929' (Speed's Airport); closed 1984. Not on today's map: drawn only if data/manual/airports has its outline and runways (see README there).

name: Miller Field
notes: New Dorp, Staten Island, Army airfield: 'founded in November 1919 and completed in 1921'; 'closed as an airbase in 1969' (Gateway NRA from 1972). Grass field with no paved runway; not on today's map as an airfield: drawn only if data/manual/airports has its outline.

name: Holmes Airport
notes: Jackson Heights (Grand Central Air Terminal): 'opened on Saturday, March 16, 1929'; 'operated from 1929 to 1940'. Built over; no USGS 1:24,000 sheet of its years: no outline, not drawn.

name: North Beach Airport
notes: Predecessor of LaGuardia on the site of the Gala Amusement Park: private seaplane base and Glenn H. Curtiss Airport 1929, 'officially dedicated Municipal Airport 2 on January 5, 1935', rebuilt as LaGuardia 1937-39. No outline traced: not drawn (LaGuardia's pavement starts 1939).

name: Newark Liberty International Airport
notes: 'Construction ... began on April 1, 1928 ... a land reclamation project to create 68 acre of level ground ... upon which a 1600 ft runway was to be laid. The airport opened on October 1, 1928, dubbed the Newark Metropolitan Airport.' Army 1941-46, Port Authority from 1948. Runways, taxiways and terminal aprons by period: data/manual/airports/pavement_dates.csv (airport EWR, tools/ewr.py): 4R/22L November 1952, 4L/22R 1970, 11/29 by 1951 (ESTIMATED), Terminals A / B 1973, C 1988, new A 2022; the runways of 1928-1952 (the first 1,600 ft runway, 1/19, 6/24) are gone and NOT traced. Runways 150 ft wide ('4L/22R: 11,000 x 150 ft').

name: Teterboro Airport
notes: 'Walter C. Teter (1863-1929) acquired the property in 1917 ... The first flight from the present airport site was made in 1919' (marked citation needed in the article; category: airports established in 1919). Port Authority from 1949. Today's two runways ('Runway 6-24 is 6,013 ft long and 150 ft wide') are drawn from 1919: their years were not found (ESTIMATED).

name: Westchester County Airport
notes: 'Westchester County Airport was built during World War II in 1942 as a home to an Air National Guard unit'; 'The first scheduled airline flights were by American Airlines in late 1949'. Runways '16/34 is 6,549 by 150 ft and 11/29 is 4,451 by 150 ft', both from 1942 (ESTIMATED: later lengthenings and the 1995 terminal apron are not separated).

name: Essex County Airport
notes: ESTIMATED: 'In April 1929 Essex Airport Corporation was formed by Walter Marvin and six other individuals. The intention of the company was to open an airport to serve Montclair' (Marvin Airport); the opening day is not in the article. Today's paved runways are drawn from 1929 (their years were not found).

name: Linden Airport
notes: 'Construction of Linden Airport was started in the spring of 1942 and completed by October 1942' (Eastern Aircraft's Wildcat plant). 'The original airport with its intersecting runways and large hangar remained intact until 1998' — the runways removed in 1998 are not traced; 'runway, 9/27, is 4,140 by 100 feet'.
